descriptor_rules.name: minimal_required_members_only
descriptor_rules.why: only the required members: every optional member is absent, which normalises to null (ex and xp absent mean the defaults: no timer, export allowed)

descriptor_rules.name: trailing_whitespace

descriptor_rules.name: pretty_printed

descriptor_rules.name: unknown_members_ignored

descriptor_rules.name: depth_5_arrays_in_unknown_member

descriptor_rules.name: utf8_invalid_byte_in_nm
descriptor_rules.why: the descriptor is the bytes as decrypted: invalid UTF-8 is bad_descriptor, and no decoder may substitute U+FFFD or strip a byte order mark before the check (a UTF-16 string with an unpaired surrogate is not valid UTF-8 either): 0xFF is never valid

descriptor_rules.name: utf8_truncated_sequence_in_nm
descriptor_rules.why: the descriptor is the bytes as decrypted: invalid UTF-8 is bad_descriptor, and no decoder may substitute U+FFFD or strip a byte order mark before the check (a UTF-16 string with an unpaired surrogate is not valid UTF-8 either): a lead byte 0xC3 cut off by the closing quote

descriptor_rules.name: utf8_overlong_encoding_in_nm
descriptor_rules.why: the descriptor is the bytes as decrypted: invalid UTF-8 is bad_descriptor, and no decoder may substitute U+FFFD or strip a byte order mark before the check (a UTF-16 string with an unpaired surrogate is not valid UTF-8 either): 0xC0 0xAF is an overlong slash

descriptor_rules.name: utf8_encoded_surrogate_in_nm
descriptor_rules.why: the descriptor is the bytes as decrypted: invalid UTF-8 is bad_descriptor, and no decoder may substitute U+FFFD or strip a byte order mark before the check (a UTF-16 string with an unpaired surrogate is not valid UTF-8 either): the three bytes ED A0 80 are an encoded surrogate

descriptor_rules.name: utf8_above_max_code_point_in_nm

descriptor_rules.why: numbers inside unknown members are checked against the JSON grammar of RFC 8259 and never converted: a library must not turn them into a double or an integer, so they can neither overflow nor be rejected (-0 is not an integer of the format, but unknown members are not read)

descriptor_rules.name: unknown_member_fraction_and_exponent
descriptor_rules.why: numbers inside unknown members are checked against the JSON grammar of RFC 8259 and never converted: a library must not turn them into a double or an integer, so they can neither overflow nor be rejected

descriptor_rules.name: tok_unknown_scalar_members_ok
descriptor_rules.why: the token object holds scalar members only: unknown scalar members (the server adds scope) are ignored

descriptor_rules.name: tok_unknown_object_member
descriptor_rules.why: the token object holds scalar members only (so th.src.tok stays at depth 4): an object inside it is bad_descriptor

descriptor_rules.name: tok_unknown_array_member
descriptor_rules.why: an array inside the token object is bad_descriptor too

descriptor_rules.name: kind_unknown_value
descriptor_rules.why: within version 2 an unknown kind stays bad_descriptor (a future incompatible change bumps the version instead)

descriptor_rules.name: kind_thumb_with_th
descriptor_rules.why: a descriptor of kind thumb carries no th: a top-level one that does is bad_descriptor

descriptor_rules.name: first_member_is_not_qa_file
descriptor_rules.why: member order is free for the validator: this text is text at the recognition step (see the recognition vector first_member_differs) and a valid descriptor here

descriptor_rules.name: escaped_qa_file_name_is_valid
descriptor_rules.why: the first member written with an escape is the member qa_file for the validator, although the body is text at recognition (see the recognition vector prefix_with_escaped_member_name)

descriptor_rules.name: th_qa_file_not_first_is_valid
descriptor_rules.why: member order is free inside th too

descriptor_rules.name: th_same_id_as_file
descriptor_rules.why: th.id MUST differ from id: a thumbnail is another file (here th is a complete valid descriptor of kind thumb that has the same id, key and header as the file)

builder_cases.name: minimal_direct
builder_cases.why: only the required members: every optional member is omitted, and ex and xp are not written when the sender did not set them

builder_cases.name: minimal_server_source
builder_cases.why: a server source with its token; obj and tok members in the fixed order (via, obj, tok(v, exp, max))

builder_cases.name: full_with_thumbnail
builder_cases.why: every member in the fixed order qa_file, id, k, h, sz, kind, nm, mt, src, m, pv, th, ex, xp; the thumbnail is a complete descriptor built by the same rules

builder_cases.name: voice_note_with_wave
builder_cases.why: m members in the order w, h, dur, wave (absent ones omitted); ex -1 (view once) and xp 0 are written because the sender set them

builder_cases.name: ex_and_xp_set_to_defaults
builder_cases.why: ex 0 and xp 1 are values the sender set, so they are written (absent and default are different for a builder)

builder_cases.name: m_without_members_is_omitted
builder_cases.why: an m with no member set is not written (no empty object)

builder_cases.name: empty_wave_is_written
builder_cases.why: a wave that is present and empty is written as an empty array (it is not absent)

builder_cases.name: empty_strings_are_absent
builder_cases.why: an empty nm, mt or pv carries nothing: it is omitted, and null is never written

builder_cases.name: strings_needing_escapes
builder_cases.why: only the quote, the backslash and the C0 controls are escaped (short forms for backspace, form feed, newline, carriage return and tab, backslash-u00xx with lowercase hex for the rest); the slash, DEL, <, >, &, U+2028 and every non-ASCII character are written raw as UTF-8

builder_cases.name: nm_cut_at_a_character_boundary
builder_cases.why: 400 bytes of two-byte characters: nm is cut to at most 255 bytes without splitting a character, which leaves 127 characters (254 bytes)

builder_cases.name: nm_cut_before_a_four_byte_character
builder_cases.why: 253 ASCII bytes then a four-byte character (257 bytes): the whole character goes, not part of it

builder_cases.name: nm_of_exactly_255_bytes_is_kept
builder_cases.why: 251 ASCII bytes and a four-byte character are exactly 255 bytes: nothing is cut

builder_cases.name: nm_three_byte_character_ending_at_255_is_kept
builder_cases.why: 252 ASCII bytes and a three-byte character end exactly at the 255-byte cut: the character stays

builder_cases.name: nm_three_byte_character_crossing_255_is_dropped
builder_cases.why: 253 ASCII bytes and a three-byte character cross the 255-byte cut (256 bytes): the whole character goes

builder_cases.name: nm_cut_counts_raw_bytes_not_escaped_ones
builder_cases.why: the cut counts the raw UTF-8 bytes of nm, not its escaped form: 300 U+0001 are cut to 255, which are written as 255 six-character escapes

builder_cases.name: mt_cut_at_128_bytes
builder_cases.why: 129 bytes: mt is cut to 128 bytes, at a character boundary

builder_cases.name: nm_unpaired_surrogates_become_fffd
builder_cases.why: nm given as UTF-16 code units (for a platform whose strings can hold an unpaired surrogate; a platform that cannot skips this case): each unpaired surrogate becomes U+FFFD, a valid pair stays one character

builder_cases.name: mt_unpaired_surrogate_becomes_fffd
builder_cases.why: the same for mt

builder_cases.name: largest_integers_in_plain_decimal
builder_cases.why: integers are written in plain decimal form, negative ones with a minus sign, up to 2^53 - 1

builder_cases.name: thumbnail_with_direct_source
builder_cases.why: a thumbnail built by the same rules, with its own src

builder_cases.name: server_strings_written_exactly_as_returned
builder_cases.why: src.obj and tok.v are copied as the server returned them (lowercase, a-f digits): never re-formatted through a UUID type or a number type (Swift uuidString is upper case)

builder_cases.name: size_limit_wave_is_dropped_first
builder_cases.why: the canonical text would be 8192 bytes or more: m.wave is dropped first, and because the text then fits, nothing else is (m keeps w, h and dur)

builder_cases.name: size_limit_dropped_wave_leaves_m_omitted
builder_cases.why: m holds only the wave: when the wave is dropped, m has no other member, so m is omitted altogether (no empty object)

builder_cases.name: size_limit_wave_then_pv_are_dropped
builder_cases.why: still 8192 bytes or more without m.wave: pv is dropped next, and then the text fits, so th stays

builder_cases.name: size_limit_wave_pv_then_th_are_dropped
builder_cases.why: still 8192 bytes or more without m.wave and pv: th is dropped last, and then the text fits; a builder that does not fit even then refuses to send

builder_cases.name: src_message_server_source
builder_cases.why: qa_file_src: the members qa_file_src, id, src, with src built as in a descriptor

builder_cases.name: src_message_direct_source
builder_cases.why: the source added may be a direct one

builder_cases.name: cancel_message
builder_cases.why: qa_file_cancel: only qa_file_cancel and id

receive_order: descriptor fields and sz range -> bad_descriptor
magic, file_id == id, stream_len range, total_chunks == ceil(stream_len / CHUNK) -> bad_header
blob length == 64 + stream_len + 16 x total_chunks -> size_mismatch
each chunk: index < total_chunks (else discard), exact length and GCM open -> chunk_auth
